title: A versatile polypharmacology platform promotes cytoprotection and viability of human pluripotent and differentiated cells.
study_design: Small-molecule screening and comparative cytoprotection experiments in pluripotent and differentiated human cells.

experiments.model: Two hESC lines and three iPSC lines during cryopreservation/thawing
experiments.comparator: DMSO vehicle in recovery culture, Y-27632, RevitaCell, CloneR, or SMC4; all groups had been cryopreserved
experiments.outcome_name: Live-cell fraction by calcein/PI imaging, confirmed by ATP assay
experiments.result: CEPT was reported as consistently superior during thawing across the tested cell lines and compared reagents.
experiments.evidence_excerpt: all five hPSC lines tested showed significantly improved viability

experiments.model: Cryopreserved iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes, hepatocytes, astrocytes, and motor neurons
experiments.timepoint: 24 h for survival; 5 days for electrophysiology
experiments.result: CEPT improved survival of differentiated cells after thawing and was evaluated for electrophysiological function in iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes. The separate motor-neuron MEA comparison in Extended Data Fig. 9 (day 7, n=3 wells, p=0.5023) does not establish significant functional superiority.
experiments.evidence_excerpt: Electrophysiological characterization of iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes 5 days post-thawing using multi-electrode arrays.

main_finding: CEPT improved post-thaw hPSC recovery and also supported differentiated-cell cytoprotection in the reported comparisons.
limitations: The excerpt does not establish that CEPT directly inhibits a single death pathway; several stress mechanisms were targeted together.
DMSO as the post-thaw vehicle comparator must not be confused with DMSO as the permeating cryoprotectant.
Formulation doses are captured; thermal handling and freezing-background allocation must still be resolved at the experiment level.
Extended Data Fig. 9 motor-neuron MEA at day 7 reports n=3 wells and p=0.5023; this does not establish significant neuronal functional superiority or equivalence.
Forebrain-neuron use with 2FA is a proposed transfer/combination test, not an already validated combination.
mechanism_claim: The study measured viability/recovery; multi-pathway stress protection is the authors' intervention rationale, while direct pathway causality is not established by recovery alone.
reviewer: root; selected results checked against source XML/HTML or Europe PMC abstract

title: Ice recrystallization inhibitors enable efficient cryopreservation of induced pluripotent stem cells: A functional and transcriptomic analysis.
study_design: Three donor-derived iPSC lines in a 3-arm freezing study with 3 technical vials per line/arm for recovery; a fourth vial per line/arm used for pluripotency assessment. Separate toxicity screen used three other lines.

experiments.intervention: 15 mM proprietary IRI-I in CS5 (IRI-I5), or CS10 (IRI-I10)

formulation.compound: DMSO in IRI-I10 and CS10 arms

experiments.cooling: 1 °C/min from 4 to −80 °C; no induced nucleation; approximately 1 million viable cells in a 1 mL aliquot per 1.8 mL vial
experiments.warming: ThawStar CFT2; dropwise culture-medium dilution and centrifugation wash
experiments.outcome_name: Viable-cell recovery relative to prefreeze viable yield
experiments.result: Original 27-vial data reproduce mean recovery of 64.094% for IRI-I5, 51.237% for CS10 and 49.160% for IRI-I10. IRI-I5 minus CS10 differs by +15.871, +2.752 and +19.949 percentage points in iPSC-4, -5 and -6, respectively. The paper reports p=0.035 for IRI-I5 versus CS10; no new significance test was performed.
experiments.effect_unit: percentage points; mean IRI-I5 minus mean CS10 across three donor lines
experiments.sample_size: 3 donor lines × 3 arms × 3 technical vials = 27 measurements
experiments.source_locator: Results: Post-thaw characteristics, Recovery; Figure 2A; original recovery workbook Sheet1 G4:M30

experiments.model: Three human iPSC donor lines after cryopreservation
experiments.outcome_name: Immediate AOPI live-cell fraction and delayed growth/pluripotency
experiments.timepoint: Immediate viability; 24-hour confluence; surviving cultures after 2 passages
experiments.result: Original mean immediate viability was 85.267% in IRI-I5, 84.344% in CS10 and 80.711% in IRI-I10. At 24 hours, IRI-I5 minus CS10 confluence was −12.61, −3.59 and +3.05 percentage points across iPSC-4/5/6. The separate pluripotency workflow lost iPSC-5 in IRI-I10 during thaw/recovery and in CS10/IRI-I5 by first passage. After two passages, iPSC-4 CS10, iPSC-6 CS10 and iPSC-6 IRI-I5 were classified pluripotent; other surviving line/arm combinations were borderline.
experiments.sample_size: 3 technical vials per line/arm for immediate measurements; 1 separate vial per line/arm for pluripotency workflow
experiments.source_locator: Results: Viability, Confluence and Pluripotency assessment; Figure 2; Table 2
experiments.evidence_excerpt: did not survive the thawing process

main_finding: IRI-I5 improved immediate live-cell recovery versus CS10, but later growth and pluripotency outcomes varied by line; one line failed in all arms during recovery or first passage. Exact IRI structures are proprietary.
limitations: IRI-I and IRI-II structures are proprietary; N-aryl-glyconamide class and patent reference do not uniquely identify either material.
No CS5-alone freezing arm; IRI-I5 versus CS10 changes DMSO concentration as well as IRI.
IRI arms equilibrated for 15 minutes at room temperature, whereas CS10 proceeded directly to freezing.
All recovery arms received 10 µM Y27632 for the first 23 hours; pluripotency cultures received it for the first 24 hours after thaw/passaging.
Three donor lines with technical vial repeats; immediate live fraction is not viable recovery or durable function.
RNA collected at 24 hours after recovery versus freshly isolated unfrozen baseline; handling, time in culture and ROCK inhibitor exposure complicate cryoinjury attribution.
Full-text review used an author-uploaded pre-proof and selected captured sections; no complete local published PDF was obtained.
mechanism_claim: IRI formulation efficacy is compared, but no direct biological target inhibition or single-molecule dual action is established.
reviewer: root; primary methods/results, deposited Figure 2 and original measurements reviewed
source_version: Author-uploaded journal pre-proof; selected methods/results captured, with published Figure 2 and original Zenodo tables independently checked
source_license: Institutional PDF states CC-BY-NC-ND 4.0; Zenodo data CC-BY 4.0; raw sources excluded from Git

title: Cryopreservation of Brain Endothelial Cells Derived from Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells Is Enhanced by Rho-Associated Coiled Coil-Containing Kinase Inhibition.
study_design: Cryopreservation and recovery comparison for iPSC-derived BBB endothelial cells with ROCK inhibition.

experiments.comparator: Nonfrozen controls for TEER; exact inhibitor-control formulation not available in abstract
experiments.result: Y-27632 increased survival and attachment and stabilized TEER above 800 Ω·cm² through 7 days post-thaw; TEER reached approximately 3000 Ω·cm², equivalent to nonfrozen controls.

main_finding: ROCK inhibition improved the ability to cryopreserve a differentiated human iPSC endothelial model.
limitations: Full-text XML retrieval was unavailable during this run; concentration, timing, comparator, and numeric outcomes remain unreported here.
mechanism_claim: Recovery enhancement is measured; a direct ROCK-specific mechanism is not separable from reduced upstream cryoinjury in this summary.
reviewer: root; selected results checked against source XML/HTML or Europe PMC abstract

title: Efficient long-term cryopreservation of pluripotent stem cells at −80 °C.
study_design: Comparison of Ficoll 70-containing cryoprotectant solutions for long-term storage at −80 °C and liquid nitrogen.

experiments.model: Human H1 hESC and human iPSC stored at −80 °C
experiments.comparator: 10% v/v DMSO without Ficoll at −80 °C or in liquid nitrogen
experiments.storage: −80 °C or liquid nitrogen, with follow-up storage intervals up to one year
experiments.outcome_name: Post-thaw colony recovery and plating efficiency
experiments.timepoint: Post-thaw colony assay; precise scoring interval not transcribed
experiments.result: For human H1 hESC and iPSC, Ficoll-containing medium was tested at −80 °C against DMSO controls and liquid nitrogen; the paper reports preserved pluripotent recovery, with cell-type-specific differences in colony performance.
experiments.evidence_excerpt: Cells were cryopreserved under the following conditions: 10% v/v DMSO in the sample and stored in LN 2 (blue);

experiments.result: The 25% Ficoll 70/25% DMSO model had devitrification-related transition temperature −67 °C versus −118.2 °C for 50% DMSO.

main_finding: Ficoll 70 enabled a DMSO formulation for reliable pluripotent-cell storage at −80 °C, addressing ice-recrystallization-associated instability.
limitations: The study includes porcine pluripotent cells as well as human cells; this record retains only the human context.

Thermal model is cell-free and uses concentrated solutions, distinct from the cellular freezing medium. Source prose mixes w/v and w/w terminology for model solutions; confirm preparation basis before replication.
mechanism_claim: Thermal stability and recovery are measured physical/protocol endpoints; no direct intracellular biological pathway inhibition is shown.
reviewer: root; selected results checked against source XML/HTML or Europe PMC abstract

title: Cryopreservation Maintains Functionality of Human iPSC Dopamine Neurons and Rescues Parkinsonian Phenotypes In Vivo.
study_design: Large-lot cryopreservation of post-mitotic iPSC-derived dopamine neurons followed by molecular, electrophysiological, and transplantation tests.

experiments.model: Post-mitotic human iPSC-derived midbrain dopamine neurons harvested on process day 33 or 38
experiments.intervention: CryoStor Freeze Media; 1.25 × 10^7 cells/mL; controlled-rate cooling ~1 °C/min
experiments.outcome_name: Pre-injection post-thaw trypan-blue viability and cell phenotype
experiments.result: Post-thaw iPSC-derived dopamine neurons retained lineage markers and neurite outgrowth. In the preparation for the initial rat graft experiment, trypan-blue viability just before injection averaged 76.5% ±0.32%. This is distinct from subsequent graft survival.

experiments.model: Cryopreserved human iPSC-mDA neurons transplanted into 6-OHDA-lesioned rats and MPTP-lesioned non-human primates
experiments.intervention: Thawed cells injected without additional subculturing
experiments.outcome_name: Dopaminergic phenotype, grafting, and behavioral recovery
experiments.result: Grafted cryopreserved neurons retained midbrain lineage and supported functional recovery in the rat model; monkey grafts retained mature dopaminergic phenotype and innervated host striatum.
experiments.evidence_excerpt: prepared the iPSC-mDA neurons for injection without additional subculturing

main_finding: Cryopreservation preserved both identity and functional utility of differentiated human iPSC dopamine neurons for transplantation studies.
limitations: Transplantation efficacy was tested in animal disease models; that endpoint is transfer evidence for human-cell product function, not a human clinical outcome.
Transplant experiments have different lesion, host and follow-up schedules; the selected summary does not assign one timepoint to all graft endpoints.
mechanism_claim: The study directly measured retained cell identity/function and behavioral rescue; it does not identify a specific cryoinjury mechanism.
reviewer: root; selected results checked against source XML/HTML or Europe PMC abstract

title: Magnetic heating of nanoparticles as a scalable cryopreservation technology for human induced pluripotent stem cells.
study_design: Vitrification and rewarming comparison using inductive magnetic nanoparticle heating in 20 mL systems and bioreactor-produced aggregates.
interventions: nano-warming with magnetic nanoparticles and alternating magnetic field

experiments.model: Human iPSCs, line 253G1, in 20 mL vitrified samples
experiments.intervention: Inductive magnetic nanoparticle nano-warming; magnetite 5 mg/mL; 208 kHz alternating field
experiments.result: Nano-warming improved viability in large-volume samples; for 20 mL, one reported comparison was 67.7 ± 7.8% nano-warming versus 34.5 ± 3.6% convective warming for hiPSC line 253G1.
experiments.source_locator: Results, Fig. 3 and Supplementary Fig. S3
experiments.evidence_excerpt: For 20-mL samples, the cell viability after convective warming was 34.5 ± 3.6%, whereas the cell viability after nano-warming was 67.7 ± 7.8%

experiments.intervention: Vitrification with magnetite-loaded StemCell Keep and nano-warming
experiments.result: iPSC aggregates were successfully cryopreserved by nano-warming and expressed the pluripotency marker Oct3/4 after recovery.
experiments.evidence_excerpt: For cryopreservation of iPSC aggregates, StemCell Keep containing magnetite nanoparticles (5 mg/mL) was added to the cell aggregates at 1 × 10 6 cells/mL

main_finding: Rapid uniform nano-warming mitigated the large-volume rewarming problem and improved post-thaw hiPSC viability.
limitations: This is a physical rewarming intervention; it does not test a biological cytoprotective compound.
mechanism_claim: The directly measured axis is rewarming/viability; devitrification is the proposed physical explanation, not a separately proven biological mechanism.
reviewer: root; selected results checked against source XML/HTML or Europe PMC abstract

title: Enhancing Viability of Human Embryonic Stem Cells during Cryopreservation via RGD-REP-Mediated Activation of FAK/AKT/FoxO3a Signaling Pathway.
study_design: RGD-containing recombinant elastin-like peptide treatment during suspension and cryopreservation with survival and signaling analyses.

experiments.model: Human embryonic stem cells in suspension and cryopreservation
experiments.result: The abstract reports improved survival and pluripotency-marker expression with RGD-REP, associated with FAK-AKT activation, FoxO3a inhibition and reduced expression of apoptosis-related genes. Full-text effect sizes and causal perturbation details remain to be curated.
experiments.evidence_excerpt: improved cell survival and pluripotency marker expression

main_finding: RGD-REP is direct hESC evidence for a matrix/adhesion-linked cytoprotective intervention during cryopreservation.
limitations: Full-text XML was unavailable during this run; dose, comparator, and quantitative survival results remain null.
mechanism_claim: Signaling activation was assayed, but survival improvement alone does not prove that FAK/AKT/FoxO3a activation is the sole causal route.
reviewer: root; selected results checked against source XML/HTML or Europe PMC abstract

title: Application-Oriented Bulk Cryopreservation of Human iPSCs in Cryo Bags Followed by Direct Inoculation in Scalable Suspension Bioreactors for Expansion and Neural Differentiation.
cell_types: human iPSC lines UKKi011-A and BIONi010-C-41
study_design: One-billion-cell bulk cryopreservation in 50 mL cryobags followed by direct bioreactor inoculation, expansion, stemness assessment, and neural differentiation.

experiments.model: Two human iPSC lines frozen in 50 mL cryobags
experiments.intervention: Bulk cryopreservation followed by direct seeding into suspension bioreactors
experiments.outcome_name: Post-thaw expansion, stemness, and neural differentiation
experiments.timepoint: 3 days for biomass recovery; days 4 and 9 for neural markers
experiments.result: The abstract reports comparable viability and aggregation for cryobags and cryovials; biomass deficits relative to nonfrozen controls were compensated within 3 days. Neural-marker expression delayed on day 4 was compensated at day 9. These outcomes support process feasibility, not identical immediate performance to fresh cells.
experiments.sample_size: Two iPSC lines; one billion cells per 50 mL bag is product scale, not replicate count
experiments.evidence_excerpt: a delay of the neural marker expression on day 4 was compensated at day 9

main_finding: Bulk cryobag handling was tested as a scalable iPSC manufacturing workflow with downstream expansion and neural differentiation endpoints.
limitations: Full-text XML was unavailable during this run; formulation and quantitative post-thaw outcomes remain null.
mechanism_claim: This is process-scale evidence for recovery and retained function; it does not isolate a molecular cytoprotection mechanism.
reviewer: root; selected results checked against source XML/HTML or Europe PMC abstract

title: Assessment of the Impact of Post-Thaw Stress Pathway Modulation on Cell Recovery following Cryopreservation in a Hematopoietic Progenitor Cell Model
study_design: Post-thaw pathway-modulation experiments in cryopreserved human hematopoietic progenitor cells using extracellular- and intracellular-type freeze media.

experiments.model: Cultured mobilized peripheral-blood human CD34+ stem/progenitor cells
experiments.intervention: Post-thaw oxidative-stress modulator reported as n-acetyl cystine/cysteine in recovery medium
experiments.comparator: Matched recovery medium without modulator after freezing in culture medium or Unisol plus 5% or 10% DMSO

formulation.compound: n-acetyl cystine/cysteine; source identity terminology inconsistent
Unisol alternative freeze-medium arm, supplemented with glutathione

experiments.cooling: Approximately 1 °C/min to −80 °C in 1 mL vials at 1 million cells/mL
experiments.warming: SmartThaw until ice dissipated and sample remained cold (~0 °C), followed by one-step 1:12 dilution
experiments.storage: Liquid nitrogen at −196 °C; duration not transcribed
experiments.outcome_name: AlamarBlue metabolic activity relative to normothermic controls
experiments.result: In the source discussion of Figure 4, oxidative-stress modulation raised the approximately 20% and 43% control values to 45% and 63% after culture-medium freezing with 5% and 10% DMSO, respectively. In Unisol arms, values approached 78%. These metabolic-activity percentages are not lineage-specific functional potency.
experiments.sample_size: At least three experiments with seven within-experiment replicates; donor independence not established

main_finding: A post-thaw oxidative-stress intervention increased delayed metabolic recovery across several freezing-media conditions in a human hematopoietic progenitor model.
limitations: Metabolic readout requires independent cell counts and functional confirmation; engraftment was not validated.

Source alternates n-acetyl cystine and n-acetyl cysteine; the dose statement is ambiguous and vehicle concentration units also appear inconsistent. Resolve identity, dose and vehicle against supplier records before replication.
Technical wells were combined with experimental repeats in statistical analysis; donor-level replication is unclear.
RevitalICE in this paper is not Evergreen Everlast; no product equivalence is inferred.
mechanism_claim: Post-thaw intervention timing supports a biological-stress strategy; neither direct ice inhibition nor a single exclusive molecular mechanism was established.
reviewer: root; selected results checked against source XML/HTML or Europe PMC abstract
